sa10:1.2: One time, the Buddha was staying at Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park in Jeta’s Grove of Śrāvastī.
sa10:2.1: It was then that the Bhagavān addressed the monks,
sa10:2.3: What’s impermanent is painful, something painful is not self, and something that’s not self doesn’t belong to self, either.
sa10:2.4: Observing it in this way is called a true observation.
sa10:2.5: Thus, feeling … conception … volition … awareness is impermanent.
sa10:2.6: What’s impermanent is painful, something painful is not self, and something that’s not self doesn’t belong to self, either.
sa10:2.7: Observing it in this way is called true observation.
sa10:3.1: “Noble disciples who observe it in this way are liberated from form …
sa10:3.2: liberated from sensation … conception … volition … awareness.
sa10:3.3: I say that this is liberation from birth, old age, illness, death, sorrow, lamentation, pain, and trouble.”
sa10:4.1: When the monks heard what the Buddha taught, they rejoiced and approved.
